deck: Table Rock and Taneycomo, written like a fishing magazine — two waters, one week, nothing invented on the outdoor desk.

play.title: Don't quit at 10.
play.body: Fall is the opposite of August. The bite can last until lunch.

season.name: Fall turnover
season.why: The lake turns over and the fish don't read the same book they did in August. Crankbaits get good again. Trout streamers get good. This is the season Branson locals wait for.
tips: Windblown banks and shad-colored cranks, 8–18 feet.
Walleye on the same gravel they used all summer, just shallower.
Taneycomo: streamers and wooly buggers when they generate. Hoppers until the first frost.
A jacket in the boat. Dawn is cold before the strip is.

body: ## Hooked on Branson Low clear water on Table Rock and the predictable Taneycomo tailwater rhythm are setting up solid early-fall action. Newly stocked rainbows remain aggressive while bass on the main lake continue transitioning to deeper patterns.

Today's Play: During lower morning flows on Taneycomo, drift or wade seams and current breaks with pink worms under a float, 1/16–1/8 oz micro jigs (brown, black, white, or sculpin patterns), zebra midges, or hoppers. Switch to heavier weighted rigs when generation ramps later. Always check the schedule before stepping in the water.

## The Week Table Rock has held steady in the 911.8–912.1 ft range across the last 7 days, sitting consistently 3+ ft below full pool with minimal overnight generation and moderate-to-stronger afternoon/evening pushes (recent peaks near 1,000–8,000+ cfs in patterns). Water clarity remains excellent; surface temps on Table Rock are cooling into the mid-70s. Taneycomo has followed its late-summer/early-fall rhythm — low morning flows giving way to 1–4+ units later, concentrating trout in seams and behind structure. Recent local reports show consistent rainbow catches (20–30+ fish per trip on many days) with browns starting to show more. Carry-forward honestly: the bite has held strong through the transition — verify today's exact cfs and schedule as power demand drives changes.

## In Season Early Fall Transition. Cooling air and water temperatures have trout active throughout the day rather than just at the extremes. Stocking continues with smaller rainbows moving upstream and becoming less wary. Bass on Table Rock are shifting from summer shallows toward points, creek arms, and deeper structure. High clarity demands clean presentations; fish are fattening ahead of winter.

taneycomo.dek: Cold tailwater · generation is the whole game

now.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F below the dam). Verify at the bank.

body: This cold-water tailwater trophy trout fishery stays productive year-round thanks to cold releases from Table Rock and ongoing stocking. Generation remains the primary tactic book: low or minimal flows overnight and early morning create prime windows for wading, light-line drifting, and indicator fishing, while stronger current (often building afternoon through evening) calls for weighted rigs and drifting seams and structure. Newly stocked rainbows are aggressive; browns are beginning to show more as fall progresses.

Wade below the dam during low periods (outside the closed zone) with micro jigs, pink worms under a float, or small flies. Drift boats and dock anglers score well when water is moving — stay in the current breaks with heavier setups. Slot limit applies in upper sections (rainbows 12–20" protected; artificials only in the trophy area from dam to Fall Creek). Below US 65 bridge, a trout permit is required to possess fish. Mega worms, San Juan worms, hoppers, scuds, zebra midges, small jigs (salmon/pink, brown, white), and egg patterns are all producing per September reports. Water clarity is excellent — clean, natural presentations win. Black jigs after dark remain a reliable option. Call 866-494-1993 for the latest SWPA generation schedule before heading out.

## Why open this tomorrow Overnight cooling, any shift in SWPA generation (demand-driven), or upstream weather (possible scattered showers) can tighten the bite, change wading windows, or alter clarity and oxygen levels by morning. A stronger generation push or passing front often moves fish into new patterns as we slide deeper into the early-fall transition. Check the gage, schedule, and local reports again — conditions can sharpen quickly.
